players.product: Megtron low-loss laminates for AI/networking boards

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026): consolidated sales JPY 2,018.9 billion, +6% YoY; adjusted operating profit JPY 186.4 billion, up JPY 94.9 billion YoY with AOP increasing in ALL segments; operating profit JPY 182.5 billion - surpassing the previous record set in 1985 to mark the highest first-quarter level in 41 years. Driven by higher-than-expected sales of AI infrastructure-related businesses and adjacent businesses (FA solutions, process automation/mounting machines, servo motors and sensors) benefiting from growing data center demand; results were better than internal plans. Operating cash flow JPY 372 billion (including ~JPY 220 billion from monetization of the US IRA tax credit through direct pay); restructuring from FY2026 contributing ~JPY 35 billion per quarter (~JPY 100 billion full year).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 sales JPY 2,018.9 billion +6%; AOP JPY 186.4 billion (+JPY 94.9 billion); OP JPY 182.5 billion - highest Q1 in 41 years

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year FY2027 forecast raised: sales up JPY 200 billion, adjusted OP up JPY 50 billion, operating profit up JPY 40 billion from JPY 550 billion to JPY 590 billion, net profit up JPY 30 billion - reflecting growing AI-related demand and its spillover effects, particularly in Industry and Connect. AI-related business of Industry: Q1 sales JPY 74.9 billion, 1.4 times YoY and higher than expected; full-year AI-related sales forecast raised by JPY 40 billion to JPY 310 billion from the initial JPY 270 billion. Demand for BBU, capacitors and multilayer circuit board materials growing steadily as expected, and now expanding into peripheral areas (mounting machines in Connect, servo motors/sensors and FA solutions in Industry, semiconductor-manufacturing-equipment-related) - beginning-of-year forecast was conservative and the demand is judged sustainable, not temporary. Middle East risk buffer reduced from JPY 30 billion to JPY 20 billion; full-year operating cash flow expected above last year's JPY 620 billion with triple-digit-billion-yen free cash flow.
quarterly_data.figure: FY OP forecast raised to JPY 590 billion (from JPY 550 billion); AI-related sales forecast JPY 310 billion (from JPY 270 billion); Q1 AI-related sales JPY 74.9 billion (1.4x YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Multilayer circuit board materials (MEGTRON): responding to strong demand, Panasonic is strengthening the supply chain including MULTI-SOURCING of key raw materials like glass cloth, in addition to building new production plants - capacity expansion for circuit board materials at Ayutthaya and Sukhothai sites; management concedes production capacity expansion was the challenge and 'we converted the phase completely'. For conductive polymer capacitors, plans to expand capacity at manufacturing sites are being accelerated; capex for capacitors and electronic materials being implemented EARLIER than the original plan because demand is growing faster than anticipated. Competitive backdrop: Taiwanese players are aggressively expanding capacity in circuit-board materials and capacitors; Panasonic cites high product capability (technical leadership in MEGTRON and capacitors). Supercapacitors attracting increased attention on surging AI server power consumption - mass production of devices for external customers to start at the Chitose plant during FY2027.
quarterly_data.figure: MEGTRON capacity expansion at Ayutthaya/Sukhothai + glass cloth multi-sourcing; capacitor capex pulled forward; Chitose supercapacitor mass production in FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Raw materials and pricing: raw material/logistics prices a negative JPY 37 billion in Q1 (copper, resin and memory price hikes) and a negative JPY 66 billion expected for the full year - 'difficult to find the materials of which prices are not increasing': oil-linked resin, memories, metals (copper, silver), and device-specific tantalum and glass cloth, across essentially all segments. Price revisions/rationalization a positive JPY 54 billion in Q1 and JPY 59.6 billion expected full-year: Panasonic is raising prices not only to pass through material costs but also to lift unit prices and margins in high-demand AI-related materials and peripherals where supply is tight.
quarterly_data.figure: Raw material headwind JPY 66 billion FY (copper/resin/memory/tantalum/glass cloth); price revisions +JPY 59.6 billion FY

players.product: BBU backup battery units, energy storage systems (ESS) and supercapacitors for AI data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Energy storage systems (ESS) for data centers: strong growth continues as expected on generative-AI demand (Panasonic Energy industrial/consumer AOP significantly increased on higher ESS sales for data centers). Supply capability being expanded rapidly: cell production lines in Japan being converted from automotive applications, cell mass production at the Kansas factory planned for fiscal 2029; module production - second Mexico plant starts mass production in Q2 of fiscal 2027, third plant in fiscal 2028, with localization of the broader supply chain including power supply manufacturers advancing. BBU: full-year aim of 1.7 times or JPY 550 billion maintained, based on demand information collected from hyperscalers. Product evolution: CBU solutions (combining in-house batteries and capacitors with Industry) start mass production in fiscal 2027; preparations for mass production of next-generation BBU built for HVDC to be completed within fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: BBU full-year aim 1.7x / JPY 550 billion; Mexico module plant 2 mass production Q2 FY2027, plant 3 FY2028; Kansas cells FY2029; next-gen HVDC BBU within FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: BBU content growth with next-generation accelerators: asked about NVIDIA Rubin production starting and per-rack battery cell capacity possibly rising from 80 W to 120 W, management said the Rubin percentage will not be so high yet but Panasonic's portion will increase including capacity, and as the BBU solution evolves the unit price would go up - required output changes and the total solution expands ('it's not replacing PBU, but it's PBU plus CPU'); non-GPU demand (TPU, ASIC, including CPU racks for inference) is also expanding and is part of the JPY 550 billion full-year picture.
quarterly_data.figure: Per-rack battery cell capacity discussion 80 W to 120 W with Rubin; unit price to rise as BBU solution evolves
